management_notes: Churchill Resources executed a coherent district-consolidation strategy in 2025-2026, entering LOIs for the Golden Baie Antimony-Gold Property (TSXV-approved March 2026) and the Black Raven past-producer in central Newfoundland. The team has positioned the company correctly against China's antimony export restrictions and Canada's Critical Minerals designation. However, the May 2026 correction press release materially revised the March 2026 Frost Cove drill results: validated assay data confirmed only two antimony intersections of consequence (FC25-17: 2.00% Sb over 0.10m; FC25-27: 13.00% Sb over 0.57m), substantially below the originally disclosed high-grade results. The scope of the 'internal data compilation discrepancies' raises concerns about QA/QC protocols in an active program. Despite the right strategic direction, a persistent failure to convert years of drilling into a classified NI 43-101 resource and the data-integrity event hold the management score at 2.
geology_notes: The May 2026 correction release materially downgraded the Frost Cove drill results that supported the prior geological assessment. The March 2026 initial release reported 7.25% Sb/1.98m, 6.44% Sb/2.06m, and 4.84% Sb/1.00m intercepts; the correction reduced validated assay data to FC25-17 at 2.00% Sb/0.10m and FC25-27 at 13.00% Sb/0.57m as the principal antimony confirmations. FC25-27's 13.00% Sb grade is impressive but narrow; the wide-intercept continuity that would support a resource model has not been established with corrected data. Churchill has completed nine additional 2026 drill holes targeting Frost Cove extensions and the Pomley Cove Pond target under a two-rig program launched March/April 2026 — assays pending as of this run. The August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report contains no classified resource estimate; the extractor returned no resource table rows. Historical production at Beaver Brook confirms genuine high-grade antimony occurrences in the district, but the validated drill-data base has been set back materially by the correction event.
capital_notes: 316.7M shares issued and outstanding; 342.8M fully diluted per the April 2026 interim MD&A — a heavy structure for a pre-resource exploration company. The 23.45M outstanding options (~7.4% of issued) represent meaningful dilution pressure; the 2.625M warrants (~0.8%) are a minor overhang. Strike price and expiry details were not captured in the April 2026 MD&A summary table. No flow-through tranches were detected in the April 2026 filing; however, Churchill Resources has historically relied on federal and Newfoundland provincial flow-through financing to fund exploration programs, and future FT placements to sustain the Golden Baie and Black Raven work programs remain a structural dilution risk — any new placement would carry a 4-month hold-release overhang. The Golden Baie option agreement carries staged cash and share milestone payments not yet reflected in the current structure.
catalyst_notes: The most immediate near-term catalyst is the pending assay release from nine 2026 drill holes completed at Frost Cove and Pomley Cove Pond under the active two-rig program (first rig launched March 23, second mid-April 2026). Given the May 2026 data-correction event, the market will scrutinize these results closely — credible wide high-grade intercepts would materially restore confidence and provide a re-rating event. Additional catalyst fronts: (1) maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate at Frost Cove/Beaver Brook — management has sufficient drill data to support one and it remains the single largest potential re-rating event; (2) Golden Baie 2026 geophysics and initial drilling results expected H2 2026; (3) Black Raven LOI conversion to a definitive agreement adding a third drill front; (4) antimony macro tailwind — China's export restriction regime remains active and North American government procurement mandates for strategic antimony continue to build. The primary near-term downside risk is that the pending 2026 assay release confirms weak results, extending the credibility overhang from the May correction.
acquisition_notes: The consolidated portfolio — Frost Cove/Beaver Brook, Golden Baie, and Black Raven — represents the most coherent pre-production antimony land package in Atlantic Canada and one of few western-hemisphere Sb exploration portfolios of meaningful scale. Defence contractors, battery-storage manufacturers, and governments executing critical-mineral supply-chain mandates have structural rationale to track this asset. The May 2026 data-correction event reduces the premium an informed strategic buyer would pay at this stage; a credible NI 43-101 resource estimate remains the prerequisite for a well-anchored acquisition offer. No NAV anchor exists and no directly comparable pre-resource antimony M&A transactions in Canada are available for benchmarking. Score unchanged at 3 pending resource delineation.
analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (TSXV:CRI) holds a strategically positioned antimony-gold exploration portfolio in central and western Newfoundland — Frost Cove/Beaver Brook (historical North American antimony production hub), Golden Baie, and Black Raven — assembled against a genuinely constructive antimony supply-chain backdrop driven by China's export restrictions and western critical-mineral mandates. However, the May 2026 correction release substantially revised the Frost Cove drill results: validated assay data confirms only FC25-17 at 2.00% Sb/0.10m and FC25-27 at 13.00% Sb/0.57m from the 2025 campaign, versus the originally-reported 7.25% Sb/1.98m and 6.44% Sb/2.06m intercepts. The geological evidence base has been materially set back. The key near-term event is the pending assay release from nine 2026 drill holes (Frost Cove extensions + Pomley Cove Pond) under the active two-rig program; credible wide antimony intercepts would partially restore confidence. The heavy share structure (316.7M outstanding, 342.8M fully diluted) remains a steep per-share value hurdle for a pre-resource company. WATCH maintained: the strategic rationale and macro tailwind are intact, but the data-correction damage to geological credibility warrants caution until the 2026 assay release can be evaluated.
